From 7811ba452402d58628e68faedf38745b3d485e3c Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Fernando Fernandez Mancera <fmancera@suse.de>
Date: Wed, 17 Dec 2025 15:46:40 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] netfilter: nf_conncount: update last_gc only when GC has been
 performed

Currently last_gc is being updated everytime a new connection is
tracked, that means that it is updated even if a GC wasn't performed.
With a sufficiently high packet rate, it is possible to always bypass
the GC, causing the list to grow infinitely.

Update the last_gc value only when a GC has been actually performed.

Fixes: d265929930e2 ("netfilter: nf_conncount: reduce unnecessary GC")
Signed-off-by: Fernando Fernandez Mancera <fmancera@suse.de>
Signed-off-by: Florian Westphal <fw@strlen.de>

diff --git a/net/netfilter/nf_conncount.c b/net/netfilter/nf_conncount.c
index 3654f1e8976c..8487808c8761 100644
--- a/net/netfilter/nf_conncount.c
+++ b/net/netfilter/nf_conncount.c
@@ -229,6 +229,7 @@ static int __nf_conncount_add(struct net *net,
 
 		nf_ct_put(found_ct);
 	}
+	list->last_gc = (u32)jiffies;
 
 add_new_node:
 	if (WARN_ON_ONCE(list->count > INT_MAX)) {
@@ -248,7 +249,6 @@ static int __nf_conncount_add(struct net *net,
 	conn->jiffies32 = (u32)jiffies;
 	list_add_tail(&conn->node, &list->head);
 	list->count++;
-	list->last_gc = (u32)jiffies;
 
 out_put:
 	if (refcounted)
-- 
2.34.1

## Summary of the Patch

The patch fixes a bug in the netfilter connection count module (`nf_conncount`) where the `last_gc` timestamp was updated every time a new connection was added, even if no garbage collection (GC) was performed. Under high packet rates, this could cause the GC to be constantly bypassed, leading to unbounded growth of the connection list.

### Modifications in `net/netfilter/nf_conncount.c`

1. **Removed an unconditional update of `last_gc`** – the original line `list->last_gc = (u32)jiffies;` at the end of the function (after adding a new node) was deleted.

2. **Added a conditional update of `last_gc`** – a new line `list->last_gc = (u32)jiffies;` was inserted earlier, right after the code that handles the removal of tracked connections during GC (i.e., when an existing connection is found and released).

### Relationship Between the Changes

The two changes are complementary:  
- The addition ensures `last_gc` is updated **only when a GC has actually been performed** (i.e., when an old connection is evicted).  
- The deletion removes the previous behavior that updated `last_gc` every time a new connection was added, regardless of whether GC occurred.  

Together, they prevent the GC from being skipped by frequent connection updates, fixing the infinite list growth issue.

You are a programming expert.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
if ((u32)jiffies == list->last_gc)
    goto add_new_node;
```
```c
list->last_gc = (u32)jiffies; // after list_add_tail
```
Reason:
The check `if ((u32)jiffies == list->last_gc)` causes garbage collection to be skipped when the timestamp matches the current jiffies. Since `last_gc` was updated on every new connection addition (the second statement), under high packet rates it nearly always equals the current jiffies, so the GC loop is never entered. This allows the connection list to grow indefinitely.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
// Remove the original update at the end
- list->last_gc = (u32)jiffies;
```
```c
+ list->last_gc = (u32)jiffies; // placed after the GC loop
```
Reason:
By moving the update of `last_gc` to just after the garbage collection loop (the `list_for_each_entry_safe` block) and removing it from the end of the function, the timestamp is only updated when a GC pass actually occurs. This prevents the frequent refresh that previously bypassed the GC, ensuring that the list is regularly cleaned even under high traffic.
